source_text:
Θεμιτὸν οὖν ἐστὶν τοῖς τοιούτοις καὶ τοσούτοις ὑποδείγμασιν προσελθόντας ὑποθεῖναι τὸν τράχηλον καὶ τὸν τῆς ὑπακοῆς τόπον ἀναπληρῶσαι, ὅπως ἡσυχάσαντες τῆς ματαίας στάσεως ἐπὶ τὸν προκείμενον ἡμῖν ἐν ἀληθείᾳ σκοπὸν δίχα παντὸς μώμου καταντήσωμεν.
χαρὰν γὰρ καὶ ἀγαλλίασιν ἡμῖν παρέξετε, ἐὰν ὑπήκοοι γενόμενοι τοῖς ὑφ̓ ἡμῶν γεγραμμένοις διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἐκκόψητε τὴν ἀθέμιτον τοῦ ζήλους ὑμῶν ὀργὴν κατὰ τὴν ἔντευξιν. ἣν ἐποιησάμεθα περὶ εἰρήνης καὶ ὁμονοίας ἐν τῇδε τῇ ἐπιστολῇ.
ἐπέμψαμεν δὲ ἄνδρας πιστοὺς καὶ σώφρονας ἀπὸ νεότητος ἀναστραφέντας ἕως γήρους ἀμέμπτως ἐν ἡμῖν, οἵτινες καὶ μάρτυρες ἔσονται μεταξὺ ὑμῶν καὶ ἡμῶν.
τοῦτο δὲ ἐποιήσαμεν, ἵνα εἰδῆτε. ὅτι πᾶσα ἡμῖν φροντὶς καὶ γέγονεν καὶ ἔστιν εἰς τὸ ὲν τάχει ὑμᾶς εἰρηνεῦσαι.
thought_title: Submission and the messengers sent to Corinth
orientation: The Roman church is closing its letter, urging the Corinthians to submit to its examples and announcing the faithful men sent as witnesses between the two churches.
pass_a_gloss: It is right therefore for those who have approached such and so many examples to put the neck under and to fill up the place of obedience, so that having become quiet from the vain faction we may arrive at the goal set before us in truth without any blame. For you will provide joy and gladness to us, if having become obedient to the things written by us through the Holy Spirit you cut out the unlawful anger of your envy according to the entreaty which we made concerning peace and harmony in this letter. And we sent faithful and sound-minded men who from youth conducted themselves blamelessly among us until old age, who will also be witnesses between you and us. And this we did so that you may know that all care for us both has been and is for you to be at peace quickly.

choices.why: Keeps the physical metaphor of submission literally, matching the source's concrete image of placing the neck under a yoke or authority.

choices.english: to fill up the place of obedience
choices.why: Preserves the spatial metaphor of a 'place' (τόπος) that must be filled, which is lost in more abstract renderings.
rejected: to fulfill the duty of obedience
to take the place of obedience

choices.english: having become quiet from the vain faction
choices.why: The genitive after 'having become quiet' indicates cessation from the faction; 'vain' keeps μάταιος literal rather than moralizing.
rejected: having ceased from the vain faction

choices.term: τὴν ἀθέμιτον τοῦ ζήλους ὑμῶν ὀργὴν
choices.english: the unlawful anger of your envy
choices.why: Keeps the three-noun chain literal: anger (ὀργήν) belongs to envy (ζήλους), and both are qualified as unlawful (ἀθέμιτον).
rejected: the forbidden wrath of your jealousy
the lawless anger of your envy

choices.why: σώφρονας means self-controlled, prudent, sound of mind; 'sound-minded' preserves the compound sense without importing modern 'sensible' connotations.

choices.term: μάρτυρες ἔσονται μεταξὺ ὑμῶν καὶ ἡμῶν
choices.english: will be witnesses between you and us
choices.why: Keeps 'witnesses' literal; the men will testify to the Corinthians' response and report back, functioning as living witnesses between the two churches.
rejected: will be mediators between you and us
will be testimony between you and us

pass_b_english: It is right, then, for us to approach such great examples, bow the neck, and fill up the place of obedience. Then, once we have become quiet and left this vain faction behind, we may reach the goal set before us in truth without any blame.

For you will give us joy and gladness if you obey what we have written through the Holy Spirit and cut out the unlawful anger of your envy, according to the entreaty we made for peace and harmony in this letter.
We have sent faithful and sound-minded men who have lived among us blamelessly from youth to old age. They will be witnesses between you and us.
We have done this so that you may know that our whole concern, both past and present, has been for you to be at peace quickly.

problems.quote: put our necks under the yoke
problems.why: Source says 'put the neck under' (submit), not 'under the yoke.' 'Yoke' is an addition with no basis in Greek.
problems.fix: bow the neck and fill up the place of obedience
problems.ruling: ὑποθεῖναι τὸν τράχηλον means 'put the neck under'; 'yoke' is added, not in Greek, misleading reader.

problems.why: English adds 'yoke' which is not in the source; the Greek simply says 'put the neck under' (i.e., submit).
problems.fix: bow the neck and fill up the place of obedience
problems.ruling: ὑποθεῖναι τὸν τράχηλον lacks 'yoke'; English adds it without basis, changing the imagery.

edits.old: put our necks under the yoke, and fill up the place of obedience
edits.new: bow the neck and fill up the place of obedience

fixed: The English added 'under the yoke,' which is not in the Greek; the source simply says 'put the neck under' (submit). Replaced with 'bow the neck and fill up the place of obedience.'

polish.changed: Clarified the first sentence by breaking it into two sentences, making the sequence of actions easier to follow, and clarified that the sent men will serve as witnesses between the two churches.

last_rejected.quote: and they will be witnesses between you and us
last_rejected.source_quote: οἵτινες καὶ μάρτυρες ἔσονται μεταξὺ ὑμῶν καὶ ἡμῶν
last_rejected.why: The English omits 'also' (καὶ), weakening the emphasis that these men will serve as witnesses in addition to their other qualities. However, 'and they will be witnesses' includes 'and' which captures some of this. Actually checking: 'οἵτινες καὶ μάρτυρες ἔσονται' = 'who also will be witnesses' or 'who will also be witnesses'. The English 'and they will be witnesses' loses the 'also'. This is a minor omission of emphasis, not a major error.
last_rejected.ruling: Minor omission of καὶ ('also'); 'and they will be witnesses' adequately renders οἵτινες καὶ μάρτυρες ἔσονται μεταξὺ ὑμῶν καὶ ἡμῶν.

last_rejected.why: 'Sound-minded' is archaic and awkward; 'prudent' or 'self-controlled' would be better. But this is a style/word choice issue, not a meaning error. The word is within normal range.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Sound-minded' for σώφρονας is within normal range; style preference, not meaning error.
